_about: M3-S2 (P-380, P-425, Bake plan row 18): a filing a "Who can be in this application" line adds when its rule holds on the person's own answers, per combination, which the configured checkpoint sets through the product routes (Questionnaires › Who can be in this application; C3.6 add the fact a rule needs; Library approval; placement), as the author, the content reviewer and the Approver. Data, not code (P-319). Every quote is word for word from the official page named in it, with its date (P-170); the line, its rule and its question are Sample, Unconfirmed: expert (AGENTS rule 4). The rule asks "6 months or more": IRCC needs no study permit for a course or program of six months or less, so a course of exactly six months is asked as a yes and adds a study permit application the child may make but does not need (Sample; the immigration expert confirms the boundary). BK-16 (P-491; QA-418): a fact may name who answers it ("collectedFrom": client_questionnaire, or staff_working_view, the default) and a short "Why we ask" ("helpText"), in the words the client reads; the case officer confirms the answer as usual.

addsFiling.conditionPlain: the child will study in Canada for 6 months or more (a course or program of six months or less needs no study permit)
addsFiling.sourceQuote: Guide 5269, Applying for a Study Permit outside Canada (canada.ca, modified 2026-10-06, saved 2026-10-27, official-sources/ircc/instructions/guide-5269.html), "May my children attend school?": "Your children may attend school in Canada. You must apply for their study permit at the same time as your own." and, under "Are there activities for which a study permit is not required?": "taking a course or a program of study which is six months or less that can be completed within the period authorized upon entry into Canada."

fact.label: Studies in Canada for 6 months or more
fact.meaning: Whether this person will study in Canada in a course or program of 6 months or more (IRCC needs a study permit for a course or program longer than six months; Guide 5269).
fact.question: Will your child study in Canada for 6 months or more?
fact.helpText: Why we ask: a child who will study in Canada for more than 6 months needs their own study permit; otherwise they come as a visitor. Sample: the immigration expert confirms.
